part.text:
Fixed. The root cause: HTTP headers are logged as string arrays (`caddyhttp.LoggableStringArray`), and the filter encoder applies the `Cookie` filter to the array field — but `CookieFilter.Filter` only read `in.String` (empty for array fields), so the unfiltered Cookie header passed through (modules/logging/filters.go).

The fix rewrites `CookieFilter.Filter` to:
- Read the cookie lines from `in.Interface` when the field is a `caddyhttp.LoggableStringArray` (returning the field unchanged otherwise)
- Parse the cookies using a dummy `http.Request.Cookies()`
- Apply `replace`/`hash`/`delete` actions per cookie name
- Return the filtered values as a `LoggableStringArray` in `in.Interface`

This matches how the filter encoder feeds array fields (`AddArray` → `filter.Filter(zap.Array(...))`), so `request>headers>Cookie` filters now apply, e.g. `sessionid=...` becomes `sessionid=REDACTED`.

- `go test ./modules/logging/` — all tests pass, including `TestCookieFilter` (which exercises the array-field path)
- `go test ./...` — full suite passes, no failures
- `gofmt` clean; only `modules/logging/filters.go` modified (also removed the now-unused `strings` import)
